To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a fully convolutional network can be trained to predict paths from a combination of LIDAR, GPS and IMU data.
a fully convolutional network trained with a combination of LIDAR point cloud, GPS and Google directions can generate paths with high agreement to ground truth.

a fully convolutional network can be used to simultaneously generate driving paths and perform scene understanding from LIDAR point cloud, GPS, and IMU data, and that the performance of the proposed system is improved by using driving directions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a system that can learn to generate driving paths from raw sensor data.
developing a system that can learn to generate driving paths using only a single sensor (LIDAR) in combination with GPS IMU information and Google driving directions.
the problem of generating driving paths from real world driving data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed system can learn to generate paths in real world driving sequences that can be interpreted by humans and that are close to human generated paths.
the proposed approach is able to generate driving paths in real-time and with high accuracy, while being trained on data collected from a single driving sequence.
the proposed approach has the potential to be a useful tool for autonomous driving.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a neural network can be trained to learn a complex task by integrating several input modalities and by using automatically generated training data.
we developed a system that can generate a driving path in real time by using LIDAR, GPS, IMU data and Google driving directions, and that can be trained with real world driving data.

we have proposed a novel learning based framework to generate driving paths from LIDAR data and that has the following main contributions: (i) the use of a novel fully convolutional neural architecture that jointly learns to perceive the environment and to generate driving paths; (ii) the use of Google driving directions as a source for training examples; (iii) the use of LIDAR data, GPS, and IMU as inputs to the network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a single fully convolutional neural net trained with a large amount of data can achieve state-of-the-art performance on the task of simultaneous perception and path generation.

the use of a single network architecture that is able to learn the perception and path generation tasks from raw sensor data and driving directions is a feasible approach that may lead to the development of autonomous driving systems that are more human interpretable and that can be deployed on vehicles that are equipped with a variety of sensors.
a fully convolutional network can learn to perform both perception and planning tasks simultaneously, without the need to explicitly define a set of features.
